newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B companies to take over firm management.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B companies to take over firm management.

text.p: Shanghai Hero Co and China First Pencil Co will take over the management of two poorly-managed state-owned plants as part of the city's efforts to reconstruct the state sector, the China Securities newspaper said on Friday.
Shanghai Hero will take over the management of Shanghai Piano Co, and China First Pencil will take over the running of Shanghai Sanxing Stationery Co, the newspaper said.
The two companies, Shanghai Piano and Sanxing, are owned by the Shanghai Light Industry Holdings Co, a subsidiary of the Shanghai city government.
The newspaper gave no indication of whether there was any share restructuring involved in the arrangement.
Shanghai Piano has a large share of its market but lacks qualified managers and appropriate assets, the newspaper said.
Shanghai Sanxing has a number of well-known products including the "Great Wall Pencil" but needs to improve its management.

"Recently, with market competition becoming more and more fierce, the need of companies for good managers has become more and more evident," the newspaper said. "Meanwhile, some poorly-managed enterprises have become weaker and weaker."
The city government "has decided to let qualified managers handle the management of famous products and good assets," the newspaper said.
The newspaper gave no further details and company officials were not immediately available for comment.

The handover of the management of the two poorly-managed state firms to the B share firms is another part of the efforts of the the city government to restructure the assets of state firms, analysts said.

On Thursday, Shanghai Vacuum and Electron Devices Co said that the ownership of all its state shares had been transferred to Shanghai Video and Audio Electric (Group) Co from Shanghai Electric Meters (Group) Co, a subsidiary of the Shanghai city government. In a similar announcement, Shanghai Video and Audio Electric Co Ltd, a domestic A share firms listed in Shanghai, also said that its state shares had been transferred to the Shanghai Video and Audio Electric (Group) Co.
The Shanghai city government said earlier this year that it would encourage healthy state enterprises and listed firms to acquire large amounts of shares in poor-performing state and listed firms.
